title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text: This page covers a central result of the cohesion theory: the knowledge-embodiment theorem. It is placed here, under design, rather than under the IVP core theory, because it is a theorem about cohesion, not a theorem of IVP itself.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
1 Cohesion, briefly
Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule. Under any modularization principle that groups elements, a module has two properties:

Purity. The module contains no element from outside its correct class.
Completeness. The module contains every element of its correct class.

A module that is both pure and complete is maximally cohesive: it holds exactly the right elements and nothing else. When the partitioning rule is the change-driver rule, this recovers the IVP notion of maximal cohesion — but cohesion itself is the more general idea, defined for any rule, not only for IVP’s change-driver rule.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
2 The knowledge-embodiment theorem
The theorem connects this structural measure to an epistemic one.
cohesion(M)=(1,1)⇔Knowledge(M)=KP(Ci) \text{cohesion}(M) = (1, 1) \iff \text{Knowledge}(M) = K_P(C_i) 
A module has maximal cohesion under a rule PP if and only if it embodies exactly the knowledge its PP-class must hold — every knowledge piece its class requires, and no knowledge piece its class must not hold.
In words: maximal cohesion is maximal knowledge embodiment. Get the structure exactly right, and the module’s knowledge is exactly right, with no separate effort.
This is why the result lives in the cohesion theory. It is a statement about cohesion — it says what maximal cohesion means epistemically. IVP supplies one particular partitioning rule (the change-driver rule); the theorem itself is about cohesion in general.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
3 What maximal cohesion guarantees
A maximally cohesive module has four structural properties.

The module is epistemically self-contained. No knowledge its class must hold resides outside; no foreign knowledge resides inside.
The change radius is bounded. When a change driver governing the class’s knowledge activates, every affected element is in one module.
The module is independently verifiable. Correctness is checked against the class’s own knowledge, with no external consultation.
The module is independently replaceable. A replacement need only embody the same knowledge and answer to the same change drivers.

These are the structural conditions that underlie the benefits of modular programming under information hiding.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
4 What it does not guarantee
The phrase “maximal cohesion is correct embodiment” is easily over-read as “maximal cohesion is total correctness.” It is not.
A system has three distinct properties that this phrase blurs:

Placement — the right knowledge sits in the right modules. This is what cohesion measures.
Faithful embodiment — each piece present is realized correctly. This is functional correctness.
Dependency parsimony — the dependencies among elements are the ones the purpose requires.

These three are independent. A module can score maximal cohesion and be wrong (one element computes its piece incorrectly). A module can be maximally cohesive and faithful yet carry an unneeded dependency. A system can be entirely faithful and badly placed.
Cohesion governs the cost of achieving and maintaining correctness — the scope that must be read and the radius that must change — not whether the system is correct. A correct system may be incohesive and expensive to keep correct; a cohesive system may be incorrect and cheap to repair.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
5 The knowledge floor
At maximal cohesion across all partition-inducing rules, every knowledge piece resides in exactly one module, and the system’s relevant causal domain knowledge is partitioned across exactly as many modules as there are classes. This is a theoretical lower bound on module count — a structural minimum, not a practical recommendation. Subdividing within a class for readability or team structure is freely available.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
section: 6 Where this sits in the theory
text:
6 Where this sits in the theory
The knowledge-embodiment theorem is proved in the published paper on the nature of cohesion [1], where cohesion is defined as correctness relative to a partitioning rule and the equivalence between maximal cohesion and maximal knowledge embodiment is established.
IVP and cohesion are related but distinct. IVP is the principle that groups elements by change-driver assignment. Cohesion is the more general measure of correctness relative to any partitioning rule. The change-driver rule is one instance of that general idea — the instance IVP is built on.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
text: The cohesion series reworks one of the oldest and most abused concepts in software design. Cohesion entered the field with Stevens, Myers, and Constantine in 1974 and was codified by Yourdon and Constantine. Five decades of research and measurement followed. This page collects what the cohesion series concludes.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 1 Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule
text:
1 Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule
The central definitional result: cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule.
A partitioning rule sorts the element set into equivalence classes — the elements that belong together. Against such a rule, a module deviates in exactly two ways:

Impurity. The module contains elements that belong to a different class.
Incompleteness. Some element of the module’s class resides outside the module.

So cohesion is assessed on two axes: purity and completeness. A module that is both pure and complete is fully cohesive: it holds exactly the elements its class requires, and nothing else.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 2 One pair per rule — the cohesion profile
text:
2 One pair per rule — the cohesion profile
A system is partitioned by many rules at once: logical code structure, deployment packaging, temporal grouping, security, platform. These are not separate things being partitioned. There is one element set EE, and each rule groups it by some of the change drivers acting on its elements.
For a system assessed under kk partitioning rules, cohesion is the 2k2k-tuple of (purity, completeness) pairs — one pair per rule. A module is fully cohesive when it scores maximally on every component.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 3 Structural proxies do not define cohesion
text:
3 Structural proxies do not define cohesion
The series argues that published definitions of cohesion overwhelmingly specify structural properties of code — method-call overlap, shared-field density, connected components.
These are not cohesion as defined by a modularization principle. They are structural proxies: observable patterns that correlate with cohesion but do not define it. A survey of 24 cohesion metrics spanning five decades shows that each measures structural coupling, not principled cohesion, reporting at most one axis and only as a proxy.
The distinction matters: a metric that counts structural overlap cannot detect the actual failure mode — whether a module holds elements the domain says belong elsewhere, or scatters the elements the domain says belong together.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 4 The Γ-equivalence rule is the coarsest change-containing partition
text:
4 The Γ-equivalence rule is the coarsest change-containing partition
Among all partitioning rules, one is special. Grouping elements by their full change-driver set — the Γ-equivalence rule — is the coarsest partition that still contains every change to one module.
Every modularization principle groups by a subset of the change drivers. Therefore every principle’s classes are unions of Γ-classes, and the Γ-decomposition is a refinement of every principle’s partition. A single Γ-decomposition is correct under all the principles at once.
This is the bridge from cohesion to the Independent Variation Principle: Γ-equivalence is the change-driver concretization of the general cohesion schema.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
text:
5 The causal cohesion metric
When the partitioning rule is change-driver-assignment identity — elements belong together iff they share the same change-driver set — cohesion becomes causal cohesion.
For a single rule, causal cohesion is the two-dimensional metric
Hcausal(M)=(purity(M),completeness(M)) H_\text{causal}(M) = (\text{purity}(M), \text{completeness}(M)) 
in (0,1]×(0,1](0,1] \times (0,1]. It is one slot of the full cohesion profile, not the whole profile. Both axes are directly interpretable and map to design actions: low purity says separate elements of impure modules into distinct modules; low completeness says merge the scattered elements of a class into one module.
The metric satisfies the six necessary conditions the schema imposes on any admissible cohesion metric, and it has an operational computation procedure.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 6 The four conditions are necessary and exhaustive
text:
6 The four conditions are necessary and exhaustive
Under the change-driver hypothesis and the objective of minimizing change propagation, four conditions are necessary and structurally exhaustive:

Admissibility — every element has at least one driver.
Element Form — every element is pure or irreducibly composite.
Separation — different-driver elements belong in different modules.
Unification — same-driver elements belong in the same module.

The first two constrain the element set; the last two constrain the partition. These are exactly the four conditions of IVP. The causal (purity, completeness) pair is the two-axis criterion these conditions reduce to when k=1k = 1.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
text:
7 Where the proofs live
The derivations — that the four conditions are necessary and exhaustive, that Γ-equivalence is the unique minimizer, that the knowledge-embodiment theorem holds — are proved in the published cohesion papers: cohesion as correctness relative to a partitioning rule in the paper on the nature of cohesion [1], the four necessary and exhaustive conditions in the paper on cohesion and change propagation [2], and the causal cohesion metric in the paper on causal cohesion [3].
The knowledge-embodiment theorem — the result that maximal cohesion is maximal embodiment of domain knowledge — is treated on its own page.

title: Architecture Styles
text:
The architectural styles examined on this site, each tested against the change-driver structure of its domain.
